Just won 1st Place w/ Monid ($3,000) and 2nd Place Overall (Mac mini + Airpods) at the Y Combinator x Naïve Autonomous Company hackathon!

We built Nomen, an autonomous AI-powered UGC agency that handles the entire content creation process for brands. You give it a website, and its agents research competitors and viral content, identify what’s working, generate original videos, and handle publishing end-to-end. It also tracks performance and uses those insights to recursively improve future content, essentially automating the entire UGC workflow.

posts.description:
And the first prize at Hackathon Fulda 2026: Future Education goes to... Team Learning in Progress!

Another fun weekend of learning, building and working with a new group of people who came together for 36 hours in one shared space. But this time, the theme was exactly where I have spent more than 16 years of my life: education and learning.
Since moving to Kassel and joining Wirtschaftsinformatik Universität Kassel | Information Systems University of Kassel, I've gotten back into hackathons. I love that the group believes research should also be translated into practice. That's exactly what I'm doing in Project LIFT, where we build tools that help learners. More here: https://liftproject.de/

So, this was my third hackathon in the last six months. A friend recently asked me if I really enjoy spending my weekends sleeping on a sofa in a sleeping bag, and I couldn't say no. Come on! It's a hackathon. Unlimited caffeine and limited pizza! You go from not knowing to knowing, then present your idea to an expert jury and convince them that yes, it makes sense.

This time, our idea started from a simple observation: there are all sorts of learners who WANT to learn but are NOT able to, because of something. So let's remove that something for them, and let them generate the solution that works for them
(shoutout to Katja Pott, who first introduced me to Generative UI). I thought: maybe we do that? That's where our journey to build "morph" began: a platform that adapts to the learner.

The idea is simple: we don't need one UI that fits all. We need an empty canvas where the UI is generated to meet each learner's needs. We don't need to create new content or knowledge either. Our AI only generates the shape in which that knowledge reaches the learner, the shape that serves them best. It gets to know them through about 20 questions, played like a game where they swipe left or right. Then it searches the research papers and builds a UI or knowledge artifact just for them. And the learner can always ask for changes, adding or removing anything.

When today's technology is so flexible, why are we still bending the student?

Team: Ammar, Tobias (I am so glad that you decided to work together), Nils, Jens (Tobi, Nils and Jens were also the winning team at Kassel Hackathon 26), Jai, Halit, Abdelrahman, Simon, Kai ( ah! I want to write so much about you! You were my favorite person at this hackathon. Even though I love working with everyone, but you were sooo good!) and ME!

Thank you team Fulda Hackathon 2026 (this was the 8th edition).
Sponsors: EDAG Group, FFT Produktionssysteme, Hochschule Fulda, HUBTEX Maschinenbau GmbH & Co. KG, JUMO Headquarters, kaleidos:code GmbH, OREXES Consulting, TechHub Region Fulda e.V., your admins GmbH & Co. KG, Landkreis Fulda and others!

P.S. I am currently conducting an online experiment in learning and AI. If you speak German and have 60 minutes to participate, I would be very thankful for your support https://wissbar.app/

posts.description:
🏆 Winners of the H Company x 42 Artificial Intelligence Hackathon (Gladia Track)

In 28 hours, we rebuilt Senna from scratch, an AI agent for public transport control rooms.
The recent train tragedy in Spain reminded us how critical decisions made in transport control rooms can be.

Yet when a bus, tram, or train driver reports an incident, dispatchers still have to juggle multiple disconnected legacy software systems, follow procedures, make calls, and write reports.

Early feedback from operators was clear: work on top of their existing software systems, don't replace them. Computer use made that possible.

So we built an agent that listens to driver calls, identifies the right procedure, and takes live action directly inside existing software, so dispatchers can focus on what really matters: critical decision-making.

No new software to learn. Just AI working alongside dispatchers.

We're already testing Senna with dispatchers and have several demos lined up with major public transport operators.

Huge thanks to Grégory, Thibaut, Nolwenn, Alexis and Zakee for all the feedback and tips throughout the weekend!

And of course, shoutout to my incredible cofounders. 🚀

Demo video in the comments.

Stay tuned for what's next!

5 teams won $22k in prizes at the hackathon & startup pitches this past weekend at the Leukerbad Robot Carnival in Switzerland! the highlights:

startup pitch winners:
1. Pasha rep'd Pulsar Robotics and won $7.2k for the best startup pitch
2. Alice and Roman pitched BIPO and won $3k for second place
3. Sepehr presented Phygularity and got $1.8k for third

hackathon winners:
1. Jérôme & team built a robot that can deliver mail in leukerbad, winning 1st prize: $2.5k and a trip to china!
2. Anna & team built a robot that can clean mount everest, winning 2nd prize: $2.5k
3. Sima, Simon, Henry and Sebastián built a robot that can teach humans playing piano, guiding their hands, winning 3rd: $2.5k
4. Andrés, Liam, Jorge & team built a drone + ground robot to find lost children, also winning $2.5k

appreciate judging with Thomas, Friederike, Raphael, Dereck, Christina and Pavani!

big shoutout to Shanshan and Pedro from Edelweiss Innovation & Intelligence Institute (EIII) for hosting and organizing as well as EuroTech Federation and Young Founders Network e.V.

How did 4 people run a hackathon for 3,500 builders?

3,500 registered. 200+ projects. 150 partners. A 9.1 out of 10 from participants.

Everyone quoted the MIT study from 2025: 95% of companies got zero return on their gen AI pilots.

My guess why: they drop AI into messy data and expect magic. We build it in three layers instead.

Layer 1: clean data. Notion runs the whole company. 10,000+ tasks, every project, the sponsor line-up, my tone of voice guide.

The AI reads all of it before it writes anything.

Layer 2: automations. Forms, Notion, email, Slack and LinkedIn, glued together with Make.

One click on "approve" sets off ten steps nobody does by hand.

Layer 3: AI employees. Agents with skills. A weekly sponsor digest, offers from call transcripts, LinkedIn drafts from 500+ of my posts.

I review, then send.

I call this a super business. A 10-person team that works like a 100-person one.

It's why our events can have shuttles and full food and drinks, and still stay affordable. Otherwise we'd need 50 people.

Which layer is missing in your company? 👇🏽

#ai #automation #notion #futureofwork

posts.description:
Today we’re putting the spotlight on Dr. Alaa Murabit , winner of the 2026 WIN WIN Award. To celebrate her win, we’ve made her full interview with Stephanie Darvill available on GTW Studio.

On the Founder Stage at Tech Blueprint, Alaa told Stephanie about hearing budget figures in global security that “honestly sound imaginary.” As a physician, she thought about what those sums could do for people who still lack access to basic healthcare.

In this clip, Alaa challenges the choices that keep basic healthcare out of reach for so many people. In the full interview, she shares how she acted on that frustration by creating For Mama. The idea was to bring Muslim organisations already working in maternal health together so they could raise more money and make a stronger case for better maternal healthcare than any one of them could on its own.

Congratulations again, Alaa, on winning the 2026 WIN WIN Sustainability Award, and thank you for sharing the story behind your work with us at Tech Blueprint.

Watch the full interview on GTW Studio. https://lnkd.in/dGYpZdQi
